goal: Iske baad aap pointer declare kar sakte hain, usay & se kisi variable par point karwa sakte hain, * se us variable ko pointer ke zariye parh aur badal sakte hain, aur uninitialised aur null pointer ki ghaltiyon se bach sakte hain.
warmup: Aap ke phone mein ek contact mein insaan nahi hota. Usmein phone number hota hai. Jab aap us par tap karte hain to aap us insaan tak pahunch jate hain. Pointer ka idea bhi yehi hai: pointer mein data nahi hota, usmein woh address hota hai jahan data rehta hai. Data tak pahunchne ke liye address ke peeche jana dereferencing kehlata hai. Socho ek dost aap ko kaghaz ki parchi deta hai jis par uske ghar ka number likha hai. Parchi pointer hai, ghar variable hai.
definition: Pointer ek aisa variable hai jo kisi doosre variable ka memory address store karta hai. Aap usay * aur us cheez ki type se declare karte hain jis par woh point karta hai: int *p; ka matlab hai p kisi int ka address rakh sakta hai. p = &x; x ka address p mein store kar deta hai, to p x par point karta hai. Expression mein *p ka matlab hai p ke andar jo address hai us par rakhi hui value (dereferencing). Aap pointer ke zariye parh sakte hain (cout << *p) aur likh bhi sakte hain (*p = 75;). Pointer ke zariye likhne se asli variable badal jata hai.
howItWorks: Memory picture mein arrows ko follow karein. Pehle aam variables ko values milti hain. Phir ek pointer banta hai aur usay & se address diya jata hai. Ek arrow dikhata hai ke woh kis par point kar raha hai. Star se ehtiyat karein kyunke iske DO matlab hain. Declaration mein, int *p; mein, * sirf yeh batata hai ke p pointer hai. Expression mein *p ka matlab hai us address par jao aur wahan jo hai usay use karo. Har pointer ki ek type hoti hai: int * int par point karta hai, double * double par, char * char par, aur type variable se match karni chahiye. Uninitialised pointer mein koi random address hota hai, is liye usay use karne se program crash ho sakta hai. Is liye pointer ko shuru mein ya to address do ya nullptr (iska matlab hai koi address nahi). Jis pointer ke null hone ka imkaan ho usay dereference karne se pehle check karein: if (p != nullptr). Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke int *a, b; mein sirf a pointer banta hai. Do pointers ke liye int *a, *b; likhein. Aakhir mein, pointer khud bhi ek variable hai jis ka apna address hota hai, aur aap usay baad mein kahin aur point kara sakte hain: p = &b; arrow ko hila deta hai lekin kisi variable ko nahi badalta.
